title: Customer capacity briefing and SLA negotiation template for Dedicated
creator: Anya Patel
summary: Create a reusable briefing and negotiation template to standardize intake conversations with enterprise customers requesting Reserved/Dedicated capacity. The doc should capture target SLA language, reserved throughput proposals, GPU-class guidance, burst/preemption policy options, and a walk-through checklist for sales/solutions teams.
background: We currently handle enterprise Dedicated intake ad-hoc: different teams offer varying SLA wording, inconsistent reserved throughput units, and unclear GPU family recommendations. That leads to long negotiation cycles, mismatched expectations, and downstream eng rework. This template aims to shorten cycles, reduce rework, and make commitments predictable.
goals: Provide a single-source briefing template for sales/solutions and PMs to use during customer intake
Standardize SLA target language across latency and availability tiers
Offer defensible reserved throughput profiles with GPU-family mappings and cost control knobs
Document acceptable burst and preemption policies customers can opt into
Produce a negotiation checklist and sign-off criteria to hand off to engineering and SRE
scope: Template covers Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) enterprise onboarding requests
Includes suggested SLA tiers (latency p95, availability), reserved throughput profiles, GPU class recommendations, and scaling policies
Defines negotiation options and trade-offs (cost vs latency/availability)
Includes walkthrough script and checklist for solutions conversations
out_of_scope: Hosted API pricing or self-serve credits
Deep hardware procurement decisions beyond GPU family selection
Legal contract wording — provide suggested SLA language but not final legal text
proposed_sla_tiers: Bronze: Availability 99.5% monthly, P95 generation latency target <= 400ms (small models), SLA applies to provisioned reserved throughput only
Silver: Availability 99.9% monthly, P95 latency <= 300ms (small models) with optional burst buffer for brief capacity spikes
Gold: Availability 99.95% monthly, P95 latency <= 200ms (latency-optimized variants) with reserved hot shards and guaranteed KV cache warm-state
Notes: Latency commitments tied to model family + sequence length profile; we provide explicit excluded events (force majeure, agreed maintenance windows, customer network issues)
reserved_throughput_profiles: Profile A (Burst friendly): 50 concurrent inference slots (~12k tokens/s aggregate for small models), supports 2x 10-minute burst per hour; lower baseline price, burst surcharge applies
Profile B (Steady): 200 concurrent inference slots (~48k tokens/s); balanced cost/latency, auto-add buffer for short traffic spikes with preemption of lower-priority internal workloads
Profile C (Dedicated low-latency): 800 concurrent inference slots (~200k tokens/s) with pinned hot shards per customer, reserved KV cache, recommended for commerce or real-time product features
Units: we present reserved throughput both as "concurrent slots" and as an estimated tokens/sec for negotiation clarity
gpu_class_recommendations: A100/RTX8000-equivalent: recommended for Profile A/B mixed workloads where memory and throughput matter
H100-class: recommended for Profile C or when latency p95 <= 250ms at high seq lengths is required
Infer-optimized accelerators (quantized): recommended when customers prioritize unit cost over lowest possible latency; require acceptance of small quality delta
Guideline: map expected tokens/sec and model sequence length to GPU class using the attached sizing matrix (link provided in links)
scaling_policy_proposals: Scheduled scaling: customers can define recurring windows where reserved capacity auto-scales to a higher profile (e.g., business hours)
Burst credits: allow temporary above-reservation usage paid at premium rates; cap per-day to avoid runaway costs
Preemption tiers: low-priority background jobs can be preempted to keep customer SLOs; customers can opt-out for higher cost
Fallback model routing: automatic routing to smaller model variant if latency SLO would otherwise be violated; opt-in to maintain availability at cost of lower quality
intake_questionnaire: Primary contact and technical owner (name + email)
Estimated QPS or concurrent sessions and percentiles (p50/p95) they care about
Typical and peak sequence lengths (tokens) and model families they plan to use
Required latency targets (p50/p95/p99) and acceptable availability %
Regulatory requirements (VPC, on-prem, data residency) and compliance needs
Burst tolerance: how long and how much above baseline can they accept as bursts
Cost constraints or target per-token cost ceilings
Desired rollout pattern: canary, 50/50, gradual ramp, or big bang
Telemetry and trace needs (sampling, retention, log export destinations)
Do they require dedicated KV cache persistence or cold-start tolerances?
prioritization_rubric: Business impact: ARR or strategic importance (High/Med/Low)
Technical risk: compatibility with existing runtime (High/Med/Low)
Operational cost: expected infra cost and support overhead
Time-to-value: how quickly we can stand up profile without custom infra
Compliance: requires Private/VPC/on-prem constraints increases priority
Score: combine into 10-point score to decide auto-approve vs require architecture review
rollout_and_onboarding_steps: 1) Pre-brief: Sales completes intake questionnaire and submits to capacity team
2) Internal triage: PM + Solutions + Infra review sizing matrix and propose profile
3) Customer briefing: run through proposed SLA tier, throughput profile, burst & preemption trade-offs, and GPU class rationale
4) Negotiation: capture agreed SLA language and any carve-outs; record cost and billing cadence
5) Engineering handoff: create ENG ticket with sizing, timeline, and acceptance criteria; attach sample load tests
6) Dry-run: run smoke tests with synthetic load and validate latency/availability at target profile
7) Cutover: schedule production switch and monitoring dashboard + escalation runbook
8) 30-day review: post-onboarding review to confirm SLOs and refine cache/warmup tuning
acceptance_criteria: Signed intake form and SLA tier selection stored in customer record
ENG ticket created with clear sizing, dependencies, and delivery ETA
Smoke test shows latency at P95 within agreed margin (10%) of target under simulated traffic
Monitoring dashboard with runbook and alert thresholds provisioned
Billing SKU mapped to reserved profile and finance notified
open_questions: Should we offer an explicit money-back SLA credit for missed latency targets or only availability?
What is the standard template for maintenance windows to include in SLA language? 2 hours/month?
Do we require security review for every Dedicated onboarding (some customers require HSM/KMS integrations)?
How granular should GPU-family opt-outs be (customer chooses H100 explicitly vs let Redwood recommend)?
